solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Objective of criminal carrying weapon

definitions.note: objective as an adjective: fair, unbiased

indicators.note: the criminal is carrying the weapon, so one word holds the other inside it

parts.note: criminal as an adjective means bad
a lance is a knight's weapon

explanation.surface: The aim of a crook who goes about armed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Objective' looks like a noun meaning aim, but it is the adjective meaning impartial.
explanation.definitionFit: An objective view and an even-handed one are both free of bias, so the words are synonyms.

clue.text: After a hellish experience, refusing to drink old liqueur

parts.note: a mare, short for nightmare, is a horrible experience
TT, teetotal

explanation.surface: After a terrible time, someone giving up drink turns down an old liqueur.
explanation.definitionFit: Amaretto is an Italian almond-flavoured liqueur.

clue.text: Daredevil coming up, briefly, to perform again

parts.note: advent is a coming or arrival

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top
briefly means cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: to rerun a show is to perform it again

explanation.surface: A stuntman is shortly coming back to do his act again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' cuts RERUN to RERU, and 'up' turns it to URER.
explanation.definitionFit: A daredevil is a reckless risk-taker, one who seeks out dangerous exploits.

clue.text: Something to blow about, primate's handling large fine

parts.note: C, short for circa, about

indicators.note: handling as holding in the hands, so the primate's word holds the others inside

parts.note: orang's, of an orang-utan
A1 means first-rate, read as AI

explanation.surface: Something about to blow up as an ape deals with a large fine.
explanation.definitionFit: The cor anglais is a woodwind instrument, a tenor oboe that the player blows into.

clue.text: These linguists are keen gardeners?

parts.note: keen gardeners ..., and the word for bilingual people sounds like that phrase

explanation.surface: A wry suggestion that some language experts love gardening.
explanation.definitionFit: Diglots are people fluent in two languages, from Greek glotta, tongue.

clue.text: Came by bike? Or by boat? Or motorway, if picked up?

indicators.note: picked up as in heard, so the words are judged by ear

parts.note: came by boat is rowed, and a motorway is a road; both are heard the same

explanation.surface: Questions about how someone travelled: bicycle, boat or the motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: A triple pun: came by boat (rowed) and motorway (road) both sound like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who came by bike travelled on a bicycle, riding it.

clue.text: Girl is deaf, missing tips

indicators.note: missing tips means the phrase loses its first and last letters

parts.note: someone deaf can't hear

explanation.surface: A girl is hard of hearing, missing the advice given.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tips' looks like advice; it means ends, so CAN'T HEAR loses C and R.
explanation.definitionFit: Anthea is a girl's name, of Greek origin meaning flowery.

clue.text: The solver emphatically in good form?

definitions.meaning: the emphatic form of you, addressed to the person solving
feeling ... again means back to normal, well

explanation.surface: Telling the solver, with emphasis, that they are in fine shape.
explanation.definitionFit: Being back to normal after illness is feeling oneself again, so the reflexive pronoun fits.

clue.text: Opera, one performed without me love!

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: the word for performed goes round me

parts.note: something performed is done
love is nil in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: An opera-goer exclaims that a piece was performed without them, my love.
explanation.definitionFit: Idomeneo is a Mozart opera about a king of Crete, an example of the class named.

clue.text: Letting go right before audience, person who flourishes

indicators.note: said before an audience, so the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: one who flourishes a flag or sword waves it, so is a waver

explanation.surface: A performer brandishing something before a crowd, letting go of the right side.
explanation.definitionFit: A waiver is the act of giving up a legal right or claim voluntarily.

clue.text: Sort of track something boring, if listened to

indicators.note: listened to means the words are taken by ear, not spelling

parts.note: an awl is a tool for boring holes; if in the sense of whether, as in 'ask if he is coming'

explanation.surface: A dull kind of racetrack, if you hear it described.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boring' looks like dull, but it means making holes.
explanation.definitionFit: An all-weather track is a racecourse surface usable in any conditions.

clue.text: It may stand in the way, note

indicators.note: one piece sits in the other, inside the word for way

parts.note: the set of something is its way or manner of lying, as in the set of his jaw
T, short for te, a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Something that may stand in your path, a note warns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stand in the way' reads as a single phrase meaning obstruct; the definition stops at 'stand'.
explanation.definitionFit: Stet is a proofreader's mark meaning let the deleted text stand after all.

clue.text: He met Agnes sneakily in the garden

indicators.note: sneakily suggests something done in a crafty, roundabout way, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man meets a woman called Agnes in secret in a garden.
explanation.definitionFit: Gethsemane is the garden outside Jerusalem where Jesus prayed before his arrest.

clue.text: Potentially dangerous steps end with cowards running

indicators.note: running as in running away in disorder, so the letters scatter and reform

explanation.surface: Risky manoeuvres finish with the cowards fleeing.
explanation.definitionFit: A sword dance is a folk dance stepped over or among blades, which could injure a dancer.

clue.text: Old bags one put in train, turning up somewhere in Pacific

indicators.note: these pieces are put in the reversed word for train
in a down clue, turning up means the word for train is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to train a gun is to aim it
one is the Roman numeral I
crones are old bags, unpleasant old women

explanation.surface: Old luggage and a lone traveller loaded on a train bound for the Pacific.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bags' looks like luggage but means unpleasant women; 'turning up' makes AIM into MIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Micronesia is a region of small islands in the western Pacific Ocean.

clue.text: Act to help penurious soldier, 20, to catch Irish girl

indicators.note: the outer piece catches and holds the other piece inside it

parts.note: a soldier who is imprisoned (the answer to 20) is a POW, prisoner of war
Orla is an Irish girl's name

explanation.surface: A law to help a poor captured soldier capture an Irish girl.
explanation.definitionFit: The Poor Law was English legislation governing relief for paupers, a statute aiding the destitute.

clue.text: Damage shower, adjusting cold tap: endless grief

indicators.note: adjusting means changing the setting of the letters, rearranging them

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap

indicators.note: endless means the word loses its last letter

explanation.surface: A broken shower, with someone fiddling with the cold tap in endless frustration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Damage' is slang for cost, as in 'what's the damage?'; 'shower' is one who shows, not a bathroom fitting.
explanation.definitionFit: A label showing what an item costs displays the price, the damage informally.

clue.text: Punch back of leg and hide

parts.note: to punch is to box
the calf is the back of the lower leg

explanation.surface: Hit someone in the back of the leg and then go into hiding.
explanation.definitionFit: Box calf is a chrome-tanned calfskin leather, so a hide.

clue.text: Give impression of being keen on probe

parts.note: to look happy is to give the impression of being so
into, as in really into jazz

explanation.surface: Seeming keen on an investigation.
explanation.definitionFit: To look into a matter is to investigate it, the verb sense of probe.

clue.text: Rarely seen clasps can bind?

indicators.note: the rearranged letters clasp the toilet word between them
rarely in the sense of unusually, so the letters appear in an unusual order

parts.note: can and lav are both slang for a toilet

explanation.surface: Seldom-seen fasteners that can tie things up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can' is not the verb but slang for toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: To enslave someone is to bind them into servitude, a figurative tie.

clue.text: Given time, one's inclined to accept one's daughter

parts.note: one's as one is, I'm

indicators.note: the word for inclined accepts the next piece into its middle

parts.note: prone means inclined, liable
one's as one is, read as I is

explanation.surface: Someone inclined to welcome their daughter, given time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Given time' is slang for being sentenced to prison.
explanation.definitionFit: A convict who is given time is sentenced to a spell in jail, locked up.

clue.text: Latin local glad as opponent's showing up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up says the letters are read from bottom to top
the letters are showing, on display within the run of words glad as opponent's

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Being pleased as one's rival is shown up.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft gave 'showing up' to the reversal alone; 'showing' marks the hidden letters and 'up' turns them. 'local' is British slang for a neighbourhood pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A posada is an inn in Spain or Latin America, the counterpart of a British pub.

clue.text: He passed on watch in return for old coin

parts.note: OB, short for Latin obiit, he died

indicators.note: in return says the word for watch is read backwards

parts.note: lo, an old word meaning look or watch

explanation.surface: A dying man handed on his watch in exchange for an old coin.
explanation.definitionFit: An obol was a small silver coin of ancient Greece.

clue.text: Alias agent used in part of this country

indicators.note: used in the sense of worked over, so these letters are reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: A spy working under a false name somewhere in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: East Anglia is the region of eastern England containing Norfolk and Suffolk, a region of Britain.

clue.text: Shots that some doctors give, bending over

indicators.note: bending over as in folding back on itself, so the word turns round

parts.note: spin doctors give spin, a slanted account of the news

explanation.surface: Injections that certain physicians give, while stooping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doctors' looks like physicians giving injections; they are spin doctors.
explanation.definitionFit: A nip or a shot is a small measure of spirits.

clue.text: What the righteous have initially got going, gradually

parts.note: the righteous have no sin

indicators.note: initially picks out the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: What virtuous people first got moving, bit by bit.
explanation.definitionFit: To nose forward is to edge ahead slowly and cautiously, as a car at a junction.

clue.text: Cold War leader's fall within a month …

indicators.note: the word for fall sits within the month's abbreviation

parts.note: NOV is short for November
a fall is a drop

explanation.surface: A Soviet leader's downfall came within a month.
explanation.definitionFit: Yuri Andropov led the Soviet Union in 1982-84, a Cold War head of state.

clue.text: … a lift to his opposite number?

definitions.text: a lift to his opposite number?

parts.words: a lift to his opposite number?
parts.note: following on from the Soviet leader, his opposite number is the American president, whose word for a lift differs from the British one

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: giving a ride to his Western counterpart.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links to 26: 'lift' looks like giving a ride, but it is the British word for what Americans call by another name.
explanation.definitionFit: Americans call a lift by this name, so it is what the US counterpart would say.
